subject: Sizing check: Silversparc dedicated commit & latency planning
summary: Customer sent a detailed traffic forecast and SLO target. We proposed model variants and a recommended committed GPU slab with headroom and fallback options; routed to CS/SE for runbook and test harness. Next: 30-min alignment call to lock model choice and finalize commit and PoC plan.
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@silversparc.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@silversparc.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial forecast + SLO targets for Dedicated commit

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is the forecast and the SLO matrix the architecture team asked for (silversparc-forecast.xlsx, silversparc-slo-matrix.pdf). High level notes:

- Expected monthly token volume: ~180M tokens (month 1 steady-state after ramp).
- Typical request size: 700 tokens output, 120 tokens input (avg).
- Steady-state traffic: ~2,800 tokens/sec (sustained).
- Peak traffic (marketing surge windows): ~9,000 tokens/sec for ~8–12 minute bursts (we see this pattern daily).
- Desired SLO: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 750ms for 800-token responses (we understand this is tight).

Two questions for you: 1) what committed slab (GPU count + SKU) should we contract for to meet steady-state + peak with reasonable headroom, and 2) if we pick a larger model for quality, how much more slab do we need?

I can set up a procurement/technical call; Marco (cc'd) will be on the contract side.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product Infrastructure
Silversparc

Attachments: silversparc-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet), silversparc-slo-matrix.pdf (pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@silversparc.com>
Cc: Marco Chen <marco.chen@silversparc.com>, Procurement Team <procure@silversparc.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial forecast + SLO targets for Dedicated commit

Elena — thanks for the detailed forecast and the SLO file, this is exactly what we need. Quick read and high-level recommendation below; attaching a quick Excel breakdown (silversparc-sizing-breakdown.xlsx).

Key assumptions I used for the sizing exercise:
- Two model options you mentioned in the demo:
  * llama2-13b-8bit (quantized) — ~1,200 tokens/sec per H100 GPU under our continuous-batching runtime (measured at 512-token batched evaluations). p95 generate latency ~300–380ms for 512 token windows; scales roughly linearly with token length.
  * llama2-70b-8bit (quantized) — ~320 tokens/sec per H100 GPU. p95 generate latency ~580–700ms for 512 token windows.
- Batching and KV/prefix caching: typical production batching for conversational workloads reduces effective tokens/sec needs by ~15–25% depending on user concurrency patterns. I modeled a conservative 15% benefit.
- Safety/headroom: aim for ~30% buffer on top of modeled peak to preserve latency SLO during onioning (traffic spikes, degraded kernels).

Sizing math (rounded):
- Target peak after 15% batching benefit: 9,000 * 0.85 = 7,650 tokens/sec effective.
- If we standardize on 13B (1,200 tps per GPU): baseline GPUs = ceil(7,650 / 1,200) = 7 GPUs. With 30% headroom -> ~10 GPUs. I recommend committing a 12-GPU slab (H100) to allow rolling upgrades, spare for autoscale, and to account for slightly longer outputs.
- If we choose 70B (320 tps per GPU): baseline GPUs = ceil(7,650 / 320) = 24 GPUs. With 30% headroom -> ~31 GPUs. Recommendation: we would not recommend 70B for a pure committed slab unless quality gains justify the ~3x increase in committed capacity; instead consider hybrid: committed 13B slab + on-demand 70B for specific high-quality paths.

Operational notes / fallbacks:
- We can configure model routing so inference for non-critical paths uses a smaller quantized variant (13B) and premium flows hit 70B (on-demand). That reduces committed exposure while preserving quality for a subset of traffic.
- If you prefer cost-minimization, we can also explore planned quiet-hours autoscale policies and a slightly higher batching target to reduce committed GPUs to ~9, but that increases risk to the SLO during unpredicted spikes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Lock model choice (13B committed vs hybrid).
2) SE-run synthetic peak test with your representative prompt set (we'll need the top 50 prompts).
3) Finalize docu/signature for the 12-GPU H100 monthly commit.

I've looped in Rachel (CS) and Kimberly (Solutions) to scope the runbook + test harness.

- Aditya
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Rachel / Kimberly — forwarding Elena's forecast and my sizing write-up. Can you take point on the test plan and runbook? Requests below: 

- Rachel: can CS validate the 750ms p95 SLO expectation against your production experience? Specifically whether we should recommend an additional 5–10% headroom for middleware/networking.
- Kimberly: can Solutions produce a light synthetic harness (k6 + small script) that replays the top-50 prompts from the forecast and produces p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec profiles at ramp to 9,000 tps? We need the harness by Tuesday so we can schedule a smoke run in the staging slab.

Also flagging a gating item: procurement will want cost comparisons for 12-H100 committed vs 12-A100 (if A100 SKU is materially cheaper, we should show tradeoffs in latency and throughput).

Thanks — cc'ing Elena for visibility.

- Aditya
